reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 13 and targeted source panel crop, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native cap/frame and note/right-edge crops, full white/cyan/alpha sheet and evidence, and unchanged naiwa.png; checked cap emblems, covered hair, brows, absence of facial hair and glasses, one mouth, three-quarter presentation, red standing collar without tie, note rows/tab, original crop/frame silhouette, backing and transparency.

remaining_reasons: The returned cap extends far above the original photographic frame, covers the frame's upper rail and creates a new cap-shaped bulge in the returned alpha silhouette. The source keeps the cap inside the tight original crop with a complete dark frame and a frame/note-shaped exterior. Restore the original cap placement, tight crop and complete frame; do not let the portrait break through the upper frame or replace the original card silhouette.

The source's small dark right-edge note tab is replaced in the native return by a triangular paper notch/fold rather than the original compact dark tab. Restore the source tab's original position, shape and dark edge construction without substituting a torn notch or new hardware.
entries.positive_observation: The dark olive cap retains two separated gold front insignia elements, gold braid/piping and a glossy black visor. Hair remains covered, dark brows are present, and the face has no glasses, moustache or beard, with one serious closed mouth. The dark olive tunic retains its red standing collar and gold-embroidered red collar tabs without adding a tie. The rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk or pinching. The dark olive-charcoal photographic backplate remains opaque, and the cream note retains two upper mark rows and mostly blank lower paper. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, missing backing or working-matte ring; the cap/frame geometry and note-tab substitution remain the separate visible rejection reasons above.
entries.visible_limitations: Fine motifs inside the cap/collar insignia and note glyphs are unreadable at 65x67 and are not rejection grounds. The rejection is based on clearly visible whole-frame/cap geometry and native right-edge construction, not on tiny symbols, glyph interpretation, head-direction guessing or alpha numbers alone.
